about: Scenarios for score_dj.py (README: Scoring a DJ version). A 'vibe' test plays one start song in the target vibe and follows the DJ; a 'steer' test plays song A, follows the DJ, then searches song B and follows it again, so the only thing that tells the DJ about the change is the second search. `vibes` and `songs` are shared by reference so two scenarios with one vibe judge it with the same words. A song's `spotify_ids` are every release of it in the catalogue (checked read-only on data/dj_eval/eval.db, 2026-10-19: done, fused_v2 841 floats, owned by every listener account, and the query finds it in the listener's 10 search results); a run whose start song is another one is excluded. `prompt` is rendered from `prompt_templates[kind]` (score_dj.py --render-prompts; a test fails when they drift). `account` is a persona in personas.json and differs between scenarios: two sessions on one account reset each other's history. Bump `version` whenever a scenario, a pick count or a template changes: the scoreboard only compares entries of one version.

vibes.kn-melody: soft romantic Kannada film melodies. No mass, rap or dance numbers, and nothing in another language.
vibes.kn-mass: Kannada mass and hype songs: hero-intro numbers, big drums, high energy. No slow love songs, and nothing in another language.
vibes.hi-romantic: Hindi romantic songs in the Arijit Singh mould. No party or devotional songs, no Punjabi singles, and nothing in another language.
vibes.hi-party: Hindi party and dance songs: Bollywood club and dance numbers, high energy. No ballads or slow romantic songs, nothing devotional, and nothing in a language other than Hindi or Punjabi.
vibes.en-workout: English workout music: hip-hop, rap, rock, high-energy anthems; EDM drops are fine. No ballads, no slow R&B, and nothing in another language.
vibes.en-chill: chill English music: lo-fi, acoustic, soft indie, mellow singer-songwriter. Nothing loud, no rap, no EDM drops, and nothing in another language.

vibe: This is a vibe test of the VibeScape DJ. Follow these steps exactly; they replace steps 2 and 3 of your usual session.
WHAT YOU WANT, and the only thing you judge songs against: {target}
You are signed in as the `{account}` account. Ignore the `you:` line that `start` prints: that account's usual taste is not what you want today.

2. `search --session <id> "{query}"`. This is your only search in the whole session. Play the result that is {song}. If it is not among the results, play nothing: `review` "start song not found", and say so in your final message.
3. `finish` that song (always finish it, whatever you think of it), then give `feedback` for it against what you want.

4. Then exactly {picks} times, no fewer and no more: `next`, then `finish` or `skip` the song it plays, then `feedback` for it. Never `play` a song from the up-next list and never search again: only `next`. If the DJ says it has nothing more to play, stop there.
5. `review` the session: did the DJ play what you want, did it stay there, and what did it play after you skipped something.
In your final message give the session id and your review.
steer: This is a steer test of the VibeScape DJ: you start out wanting one vibe, change your mind partway through, and tell the DJ only by searching for a song in the new vibe. Follow these steps exactly; they replace steps 2 and 3 of your usual session.
You are signed in as the `{account}` account. Ignore the `you:` line that `start` prints: that account's usual taste is not what you want today.
PHASE A. You want vibe A. Judge every song in this phase against A only.
2. `search --session <id> "{query_a}"`. Play the result that is {song_a}. If it is not among the results, play nothing: `review` "first song not found", and say so in your final message.
3. `finish` that song (always finish it, whatever you think of it), then give `feedback` for it against A.
4. Then exactly {picks_a} times, no fewer and no more: `next`, then `finish` or `skip` the song it plays, then `feedback` for it against A.
PHASE B. Right after the feedback for the {picks_a}th DJ song you change your mind: from now on you want vibe B, and only B. Judge every song from here on against B, never A.

5. `search --session <id> "{query_b}"`. This is your second and last search. Play the result that is {song_b}. If it is not among the results, play nothing: `review` "second song not found", and say so in your final message.
6. `finish` that song (always finish it), then give `feedback` for it against B.

7. Then exactly {picks_b} times, no fewer and no more: `next`, then `finish` or `skip` the song it plays (as someone who wants B), then `feedback --session <id> <handle> --fit <1-5> --vibe <A|B|other> --reason "..."`. `--fit` is how well the song fits B. `--vibe` says which vibe the song itself belongs to: `A` if it is an A song, `B` if it is a B song, `other` if it is neither; if it could be either, pick the closer one. Every song in this step needs `--vibe`.
In both phases: never `play` a song from the up-next list, and never search except in steps 2 and 5. If the DJ says it has nothing more to play, stop there.
8. `review` the session: did the DJ keep vibe A, how many songs after your second search it took to follow you to B, and whether A songs kept coming after that.
In your final message give the session id and your review.
